# Manage skills and agents

One source, generated copies. Edit only the canonical files in `.agents/`, then run the generator.

| Canonical (edit) | Generated (do not edit) | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | used as is | Codex, Copilot |
| same file | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Claude Code |
| `.agents/agents/<name>.md` | `.claude/agents/<name>.md` | Claude Code |
| same file | `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` | Copilot |
| same file | `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` | Codex |

Instruction files are written by hand: `CLAUDE.md` (full rules), `AGENTS.md` (summary for Codex and others), `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` (Copilot).

## Add a skill

1. Create `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The name is lowercase kebab-case and equals the folder name.
2. Frontmatter has exactly `name` and `description`, each on one line. The description says what the skill does and when to use it (under 1024 characters), because every tool uses it to decide when to load the skill.
3. The body is a numbered recipe with real paths and commands of this repository. Reference commands as `npm run <script>` only for scripts in `package.json`, and paths in backticks only if they exist: `tests/tooling/agent-files.test.ts` checks both.
4. Do not use tool-specific words ("Claude", "Copilot", a tool name). Say "run" and "read".

## Add an agent

1. Create `.agents/agents/<name>.md` with frontmatter `name`, `description` and `tools`.
2. `tools` is a comma-separated list of neutral names: `read`, `search`, `edit`, `run`, `web`. The generator maps them (Claude: Read, Grep and Glob, Edit and Write, Bash, WebFetch; Copilot: read, search, edit, execute, web). Codex has no tools key, so the generator adds a "read-only" line to agents that lack `edit`.
3. Give the minimum tools. Reviewers get `read, search, run`; only writers get `edit`.
4. Write the body as the agent's own instructions. Do not use `'''` (three single quotes) in it: the Codex file is TOML.

## Generate and check

- `npm run sync:agents` writes the generated files and removes generated files whose source is gone.
- `npm run check:agents` writes nothing and exits 1 when a generated file is missing, out of date or stale. `npm test` runs the same comparison through `tests/tooling/agent-files.test.ts`.
- Commit the canonical and the generated files together.

Never edit a generated file by hand: the next run overwrites it.
